answer: Slow identity creation down with a verifiable delay: each new agent identity must finish a sequential puzzle that takes hours of wall-clock time before it can trade, like a dune that only a steady gale can reshape, not a sudden gust. A small deposit is locked alongside and refunded only after the agent completes honest work, so mass-producing aliases costs both time and capital. A garden of identities planted overnight cannot bloom in time to game one round, and anyone caught cheating loses the deposit and must start the slow climb again.
